content.intro: Learn RubyVM, Bytecode, and Execution Internals through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding rubyvm, bytecode, and execution internals helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: RubyVM, Bytecode, and Execution Internals helps you reason about a high-level view of ruby execution. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: A high-level view of Ruby execution. Then connect it to Instruction sequences. The remaining syllabus points—Runtime diagnostics, Separating language guarantees from implementation details—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

end
